name: Gate runner (Node entry point)
purpose: The single Node entry-point module the project realises and that any CI provider invokes with one command line. Owns the ordered execution of the configured gate set, the capture of each gate's exit code and streams, the delegation to the per-gate report writer (TAC-702), the delegation to the aggregate report writer (TAC-703), and the shape of the operator-visible failure summary written to stderr on any gate failure.
responsibilities: Expose a Node entry point (a single `.js` or `.mjs` file) invocable as `node <path>` with no shell glue; the entry point path is stable and recorded on the aggregate report's `runner.entryPoint` field (AC-6102-1, AC-6102-2, AC-6110-1).

Read gate configuration (gate set, gate ordering, report directory) from configuration inputs available equally in CI and on a developer machine; refuse to gate control flow on CI-provider-specific environment variables (AC-6110-2).

Invoke each configured gate as a Node child process against the project tree; capture the child's exit code, stdout, and stderr; measure start/end wall-clock timestamps and duration (AC-6103-1, AC-6104-1).

Run `rcf define validate` as the first required gate; run `rcf audit coverage --strict` as the second required gate; continue past a failing gate to run the remaining required gates (AC-6103-2, AC-6104-2, AC-6107-2).
Delegate per-gate report writing to TAC-702 on every gate completion (pass or fail); delegate aggregate report writing to TAC-703 on suite completion (AC-6105-1, AC-6106-1).

On any gate failure, write a single-line operator-readable failure summary to the entry point's own stderr naming the failing gate, its exit code, and the relative path to the per-gate report file (AC-6107-1).

Detect missing per-gate report files (a gate whose child process was killed, exited with an uncaught exception, or whose report write failed) and record the affected gate as `missing` with a reason in the aggregate report; exit non-zero on any missing outcome (AC-6108-1, AC-6108-2).
Exit non-zero when the aggregate verdict is `failed`; exit zero only when every gate outcome is `passed` (AC-6101-2, AC-6103-2, AC-6104-2).
internalStructure: One Node module that exports a `runGates({ reportDir, gates, cwd })` function and a shebang entry point that reads its configuration and calls `runGates`. The gate set is a small array of `{ name, command }` descriptors; the runner spawns each command as a child process (Node's `child_process.spawn`), streams stdout/stderr into buffers with size caps, times the child, and hands the recorded fields to the per-gate report writer. A finaliser catches any thrown exception in the gate loop, marks the affected gate `missing` with an exception-derived reason, and continues. The aggregate writer is called once at loop end with the accumulated gate records.

interfaces.name: runGates
interfaces.description: runGates({ reportDir, gates, cwd }) -> Promise<{ verdict, exitCode, aggregateReportPath }>; the sole callable the entry point invokes. Runs every gate in `gates` order, delegates each report write, resolves with the final verdict.

interfaces.name: gate-descriptor
interfaces.description: { name: string, command: string[] } where `command[0]` is the executable (typically `rcf`) and the rest are argv. The set-of-two required for v1.0.0 is `[{ name: 'validate', command: ['rcf', 'validate'] }, { name: 'coverage-strict', command: ['rcf', 'coverage', '--strict'] }]`.

interfaces.name: entry-point CLI
interfaces.description: `node <entryPointPath>` with no required argv. Optional flag `--report-dir <path>` overrides the default report directory. Exit code is the aggregate exit code.

dependencies.name: Per-gate report writer
dependencies.description: Called once per gate with the captured fields; writes the per-gate JSON report and returns the file path the aggregate writer records.

dependencies.name: Aggregate report writer
dependencies.description: Called once at end-of-suite with the ordered gate records; writes the aggregate JSON report and returns the verdict and its exit code.

dependencies.name: rcf CLI
dependencies.description: The underlying `rcf` binary the child processes invoke. The runner does not import rcf as a library; every gate is a separate Node process.

tradeoffs: Running every gate as a separate child process costs Node startup for each; that cost buys a stable exit-code contract and a stable stream capture surface that a library-mode invocation would obscure. Continuing past a failing gate costs a slightly longer pipeline; that cost buys the reviewer seeing every failure on one run instead of chasing them one at a time. The runner does not run gates in parallel: gate ordering is a stable property the aggregate report depends on, and the small gate count at v1.0.0 does not motivate a parallel-and-serialise design.
